# Surf Inn

> Surf camps in Brazil: Rio de Janeiro (Recreio, Macumba beach) and Itacaré (Bahia). Surf lessons in small groups (3 students max per coach), accommodation by the beach, packages, local experiences. Requests are free and without commitment; the team replies with a personal quote.

This file gives the text of the beta site https://surfinn-beta.vercel.app page by page, because the site is rendered with JavaScript. English version; French under /fr/, Portuguese under /pt/.

WHO IT'S FOR
Whatever your level, you belong here.
●
Beginners: First waves in the lineup, on easy beach breaks, three students max per coach
●
Intermediates & advanced: Small-group or private lessons and video analysis to break your plateau
●
Independent surfers: Daily guiding at the best spots, board rental can be included
●
Solo travelers: Come alone, leave with friends for life
●
Digital nomads: Coworking space and fast wifi for a real work/surf balance
●
Groups: Friend trips, couples and team retreats, we handle everything
●
Yoga lovers: Yoga lessons every day, Hatha, Vinyasa, Bhakti, included in your stay
Your trip, built around you.

## Surf camp in Rio de Janeiro

URL: https://surfinn-beta.vercel.app/surf-camp/rio-de-janeiro/

SURF INN RIO
Surf Camp Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
Surf all day. Rio all night.
Stay by Macumba Beach in Recreio, Rio's surf side, with local coaching, small-group surf lessons and some of the city's best-known breaks nearby.
Request to book
★ 4.9/5 · 438 Google reviews · Free, no commitment
A real (and probably sandy) person replies fast.
OVERVIEW
THE CAMP
EXPERIENCES
SURF PACKAGES
SURF GUIDE
WHY SURF IN RIO
Between the beach and the beat
Surf the waves of Recreio, explore the wild beaches of Rio, and discover the city's rhythm. The perfect balance between a surf trip and a city adventure.
5
Nearby surf areas
Macumba, Recreio, CCB, Prainha & Grumari. These beaches face different ways, so each one works best with a different swell, wind and tide. Shortboard and longboard waves, a walk apart.
340+
Surfable days a year
Beach breaks catch every swell direction. Small days or big days, there is almost always a spot that works.
26°C
Water in summer
Boardshorts and a lycra. A thin top for a few winter mornings, never a wetsuit battle.
1
Wave for every level, every day
Mellow Macumba for first rides, Recreio's peaks to step up, Prainha and Grumari when it pumps. From beginner to world-class waves, something is always working.
3
Surfers max per coach
Small-group surf lessons mean more individual feedback, more waves watched and coaching adapted to your level.
YOUR STAY
Surf Inn Rio · The camp
One camp, three places, two minutes apart on foot. You sleep in one, you live in all three.
·
Private or shared rooms, 40 boards, 20 of them by César Baltazar
·
The Surf Club · a hostel with a pool, gym, sauna and restaurants
·
The Beach House · a quiet beachfront pousada with a kitchen
·
The Surf House · a house of surfers and artists with a pool, yoga, percussion and boards
See the camp →
LIFE IN RECREIO
Between two sessions, a whole city to play in
Beyond the surf lessons, everything you can add to your stay: coaching, guiding, recovery, music and days out. Build your trip item by item.

Discover all experiences →
SURF LESSONS · THE METHOD
How we teach
01
Three students max
Every lesson runs with three students per coach, never more. Qualified, English-speaking coaches, and we never mix levels.
02
1h30, step by step
30 minutes in the gym first: theory, the pop-up, repetitions. Then an hour in the water, with your coach right beside you.
03
Four lessons a day
Lessons at 6:30, 8:30, 10:30 and 14:30. Coaches read the banks and tides each morning and take you where your level works best.
04
See yourself surf
We film your session, then sit down with you to review it wave by wave: stance, timing, what to fix next lesson.
See surf packages & lessons →
THE LOCATION
Recreio, Rio's surf side
Surf Inn Rio
Show the map
Open in Google Maps →
The neighborhood
Recreio dos Bandeirantes: Rio's laid-back surf quarter. Juice bars, surf shops, restaurants and beach kiosks along Praia da Macumba, with a right and a left breaking at the Recreio corner. The city's energy without the tourist crush, and nature much closer.
Getting here
Fly into Rio (GIG or SDU). We arrange your door-to-door transfer, about 50 minutes from GIG, so you land, wave, and you're on the beach.
Why this spot
From where you stay, Praia da Macumba is right in front and Recreio's peaks are a short walk; Prainha and Grumari 10 minutes away; Ipanema and the city 40 minutes when you want them.
THE REGION
Recreio, Rio's best-kept secret
Not the postcard Rio of Ipanema, and that's the point. Recreio is where cariocas actually surf, and everything below is minutes from where you stay.
‹
›
SURF
Praia da Macumba
Rio's best all-round surf beach, a proper right AND a left. Heaven for longboards, while the canto do Recreio runs fast and hollow for shortboarders.
BEACH
Prainha
A protected half-moon of sand backed by rainforest, many cariocas call it Rio's most beautiful beach. A surfers' sanctuary, minutes away, and its beach restaurant serves excellent food until 4 pm.
NATURE
Grumari & its park
A wild beach inside a protected natural park: no buildings, no kiosk chains, just waves and green. The escape when the city feels close.
LIVE MUSIC
Small Riders
The surf club right next to where you stay, live concerts Thursday through Sunday, and the whole young surf scene of Recreio in one place.
PARTY
Lua nights
Some nights the beach lights a bonfire in the sand, musicians or a DJ, everyone barefoot, singing and dancing until late.
NIGHT
Forró & the bars
Forró takes over the neighborhood most weekends, and the surf bars around Macumba fill up after the last session. A beer, live music, the whole lineup at the next table.
Real days at Surf Inn Rio
Taken by guests and the team, not by a photographer.

### Questions and answers

Q: Where will I stay in Rio?
A: In one of our three places in Recreio: The Surf Club, The Beach House or The Surf House. You choose a private or a shared room when you send your request, our team picks the place and confirms it. Your surf lessons, yoga and experiences happen across the three, run by the Surf Inn team.

Q: Is Recreio safe?
A: It's Rio's laid-back family-and-surfers quarter, calmer than the tourist zones. Basic big-city street sense applies, and we brief you on arrival.

Q: How far is the airport?
A: About 50 minutes from GIG. We arrange door-to-door transfers, someone waits with your name when you land.

Q: What if it's flat at Macumba?
A: It rarely is, and when it is, Prainha, Grumari or a surfskate session cover the day.

Q: Can I see the "postcard Rio"?
A: Easily. Ipanema, Arpoador and the center are 40 minutes away. Many guests do one city day per week.

Q: Do I need to bring my board?
A: No. 40 boards in Recreio, 20 of them Baltazar Customs, shaped by César Baltazar, from softboards to longboards. Unlimited board rental can be added to any package.

Every level has a plan
Beginner
Softboards at Macumba, our mellow home spot. Depending on the sea, we head for the lineup waves from the very first lesson, with a coach never more than a wave away.
Intermediate
Break the plateau: video analysis, punchier peaks at Recreio, and drills on the surfskate to fix your turns between sessions.
Advanced
Dawn missions to Prainha and Grumari when the swell is right, step-up boards in the quiver, and a guide who knows every bank.
How a session goes
1
Spot & briefing
Your coach picks the day's best spot for your level and walks you through banks, currents and the plan.
2
Warm-up on land
Mobility, pop-up drills in the sand, and the one thing you'll each focus on today.
3
In the water
With your coach in the lineup, three students max, every wave watched and corrected live.
4
Debrief
What clicked, what to fix, and what tomorrow looks like, over fresh fruit back at the camp.
Everything's provided
Board for your level
Leash
Wax
Boards, leashes and wax are included in every lesson, and the full quiver is there to rent between sessions.

When to surf in Rio, season by season
Waves basically all year, what changes is the size, the crowd and how long you stay in the water. The short version:
Dec – Mar
Summer
Feriados: Réveillon · Carnaval
Water
24–26°C
Air
28–38°C
Waves
0.5–1.2 m
Crowd

Beach season, small, sunny, perfect for learning. Carnival in February.
Apr – Jun
Autumn
Feriados: Tiradentes
Water
23–24°C
Air
22–28°C
Waves
1–2 m

The sweet spot: consistent swell, mellow weather, emptier lineups.
Jul – Sep
Winter
Feriados: Férias de julho
Water
21–22°C
Air
18–26°C
Waves
1.5–2.5 m
Crowd
Quiet
Swell season. The biggest, cleanest days of the year.
Oct – Nov
Spring
Water
22–23°C
Air
24–30°C
Waves
0.8–1.5 m
Crowd
Medium
Warming up again, friendly waves and long evenings.
The surf spots
Praia da Macumba
All levels
Our home spot, right opposite the Surf Club. Mellow, sandy-bottom peaks, where most first waves happen.
Recreio
All levels
Punchier peaks along the same stretch, something for everyone, every day.
Prainha
Advanced
Rio's best wave, inside a nature reserve 10 minutes away. Hollow, powerful, worth the trip.
Grumari
Intermediate
Wild, undeveloped beach next door, fewer people, more space to push yourself.
What to wear
Boardshorts or bikini with a lycra, all year.
Whenever you come, your coaches pick the right spot for the day, that's what surf guidance is for.
Ocean safety, handled
Every morning starts with a spot briefing: banks, currents, where to paddle out and where not to. Beginners surf lifeguarded, sandy-bottom stretches only, and our coaches are trained in ocean rescue and first aid.
Rio is waiting. So are the waves.

SURF GUIDE
WHY SURF IN ITACARÉ
Surf in the middle of the Mata Atlântica
One road, a dozen waves, rainforest in between. Tiririca, Bahia's most consistent beach break, is five minutes on foot.
5
Beaches on foot
Tiririca, Resende, Ribeira, Praia da Costa, Prainha. All a short walk from the house, each one working on a different tide.
25°C+
Water, all year round
Bikini and boardshorts in July as in January. You will never own a wetsuit here.
12/12
Months with waves
South swells in winter, east swells in summer, beaches facing every direction. There is no off-season in Itacaré.
1
Wave for every level, every day
Punchy Tiririca, sheltered Ribeira, long fun walls at Engenhoca. Whatever the tide and your level, the right peak is working somewhere.
0
Buildings on the beach
Engenhoca and Havaizinho are national-park beaches: sand, forest, a few surfers. That's the whole view.
7/7
A party in town every night
Forró, samba, reggae, live music. Every night of the week has its own party somewhere in town, a five-minute walk from your bed.
THE CAMP
A house wrapped in green
Right in the center of Itacaré, the best location there is: a leafy garden full of birdsong, a quiver of boards and a welcoming place to come back to.

SURF LESSONS · THE METHOD
How we teach
01
Three students max
Every lesson runs with three students per coach, never more. Qualified, English-speaking coaches, and we never mix levels.
02
2 hours, step by step
30 minutes on the sand first: theory, the pop-up, repetitions adapted to you. Then 1h30 in the water, with live feedback from your coach.
03
Every morning at 8:00
Lessons start at 8:00. Coaches read the banks and tides each morning and take you where your level works best.
04
See yourself surf
We film your session, then sit down with you to review it wave by wave: stance, timing, what to fix next lesson.
See surf packages & lessons →
THE LOCATION
Itacaré, the surf capital of Bahia
Surf Inn Bahia
Show the map
Open in Google Maps →
The town
A fishing village turned bohemian surf town: cobbled streets, açaí counters, capoeira circles at sunset. Everything walkable, everyone friendly.
Getting here
Fly into Ilhéus (IOS), 1h15 from the camp along a coastal road. We arrange the transfer, you'll want the window seat. From Salvador: an Uber to the ferry, cross to Bom Despacho, then the bus to Itacaré. About six hours door to door, and an easy one.
Why this spot
Tiririca, the town's main wave, is a short walk; four more beaches hide within 20 minutes of trail. Different directions, different moods: something always works.
THE REGION
Why everyone falls for Itacaré
A fishing town swallowed by jungle, where the day belongs to the waves and the night always has a plan.
‹
›
PARTY
A party every night
Forró, samba, reggae, live music, every night of the week has its own party somewhere in town. You never have to look far.
SURF
Tiririca
Itacaré's star wave, two steps from town, fast, punchy, and home to national championships.
BEACH
Four beaches, one trail
Tiririca, da Costa, Ribeira, Prainha, one jungle trail, four coves framed by Mata Atlântica. Prainha alone is worth the trip.
NATURE
Waterfalls everywhere
A dozen cachoeiras within reach for flat days, swim, jump, picnic under the falls.
CULTURE
Capoeira & roda culture
Capoeira was never a show here, rodas happen in the streets of town, and everyone's invited to clap, sing or play.
SLOW LIFE
Rio de Contas at sunset
SUP, canoe or boat on the Rio de Contas at golden hour, where the jungle meets the sea, the calm side of Itacaré.
FOOD
Tapioca, açaí, moqueca
A tapioca cart at the trailhead, açaí bowls after the session, and moqueca baiana for dinner. Eating here is half the trip.

### Questions and answers

Q: How do I get to Itacaré?
A: Fly to Ilhéus (IOS), then about 1h15 by road. We arrange the transfer, you land, we take it from there.

Q: Is the wifi good enough for work?
A: Yes. Starlink at the camp, with a call-friendly coworking corner. Video calls run fine.

Q: What happens on flat days?
A: A cacao farm, the gym, waterfalls, a boat on the Rio de Contas, a party in town. Flat days have a way of becoming favorite days.

Q: Do I need to bring my board?
A: No. Boards for every level are at the house, some of them shaped by César Baltazar, from softboards to shortboards. Unlimited board rental can be added to any package.

Q: Do I need cash in town?
A: Cards and Pix cover almost everything; a little cash helps at beach kiosks and small bars.

SURF GUIDE
When to surf in Itacaré, season by season
The water never gets cold and the waves never really stop, the seasons just change the flavor:
Dec – Mar
Summer
Feriados: Réveillon · Carnaval
Water
27–28°C
Air
28–34°C
Waves
0.5–1.2 m
Crowd
Lively
Sunny, playful waves and the town at its brightest. Beginner heaven.
Apr – Jun
Green season
Feriados: Tiradentes
Water
26–27°C
Air
25–30°C
Waves
0.5–1.5 m
Crowd
Quiet
Bigger swell, short tropical showers, everything intensely green.
Jul – Sep
Winter
Feriados: Férias de julho
Water
25–26°C
Air
23–28°C
Waves
0.5–1.5 m
Crowd
Quiet
The most consistent swell of the year, and still boardshorts weather.
Oct – Nov
Spring
Water
26–27°C
Air
26–31°C
Waves
0.8–1.5 m
Crowd
Medium
Mellow, warm and uncrowded, a local favorite.
The surf spots
Praia do Pontal
Beginner
Protected and gentle, a short boat ride across the river from town, where first pop-ups happen.
Engenhoca
Beginner · Intermediate
A jungle-trail classic: left and right peaks framed by rainforest.
Ribeira
Beginner · Intermediate
Sheltered and forgiving, the town's gentle option a short walk away.
Tiririca
Intermediate · Advanced
The town's main wave, a short walk away. Fast, fun beach break with real push.
Jeribucaçu
Advanced
River-mouth wave at the end of a wild trail, heavier, hollower, worth earning.
What to wear
Boardshorts or bikini plus a lycra for the sun, that's it, twelve months a year. The water stays at 25°C or more.
Whenever you come, your coaches pick the right spot for the day, that's what surf guidance is for.
Ocean safety, handled
Every session starts with a spot briefing: rips, rocks, river mouths and where to sit. Beginners stay on protected, sandy-bottom beaches, and our coaches are trained in ocean rescue and first aid.
The jungle keeps no schedule. Neither will you.

## Who it is for

URL: https://surfinn-beta.vercel.app/who-is-it-for/

WHO IT'S FOR
A surf camp designed for four ways of traveling.
Not quite a surf camp, not a hostel, not a coliving. Surf Inn is its own thing. Here's who thrives here, honestly.
01 · LEARN
You want to go home better at something
Learning is one of the best ways to live a trip. At Surf Inn, everything is set up to spark your curiosity and give you the best conditions to learn, in surf, music or any other discipline, whether you're starting out or looking to progress.
★★★★★
"Comparing to other surf camps I have been to, I'm confident to say that here I improved the most. The teachers will be selected according to your level and goal. Gamechanger is the ratio of teachers to students, which was never more than 1:3 during my stay. Besides surfing the hostel is pretty nice, offers daily activities and is located just across from the ocean."
N
Nish
on Google
02 · WORK
You work remotely and want the ocean back in your days
Surf Inn is an ideal place to work: everything is set up for remote workers. High-speed internet (Starlink), a quiet coworking corner for calls, rooms with a desk on request, and a timezone (GMT-3) that leaves your afternoons free on European hours, and your mornings on North American ones.
★★★★★
"I originally planned to stay for just one week, but it didn't take long for me to extend my stay to an entire month, which already says everything about how special this place is. What made this experience so unique were the people. I met incredible individuals and felt welcomed, supported, and at home the entire time."
L
Leif
on Google
03 · BELONG
You travel and want a place that feels like people, not a program
Surf Inn is also simply a great place for a holiday, for a few days or several weeks, without booking a single lesson: the beach, the evenings, the sunsets in Rio and Itacaré. And a natural meeting point for travelers.
★★★★★
"We spent an amazing 7 days there, in which we have made loads of new friendships whom we will cherish forever. The surf lessons, which were available through a package deal, were held in small groups so the teachers really took their time to help you improve. Highly recommend!"

on Google
04 · EXPLORE
You want to see Brazil from the inside
Surf Inn aims to give everyone an authentic Brazil and to share the country's cultural richness through all its activities, rooted in community-based tourism.
★★★★★
"The camp is situated in a small town, super authentic of Brazil: With a long beautiful beach, lots of people in the evening that are listening to music and dancing, but during the day it is very calm and chill. All surf teachers are very knowledgeable, they do not just push you into the water, but give you all the necessary informations (and theory which is very useful) to learn surfing the best way."

on Google
E AÍ, BRASILEIRO?
Isso aqui também é seu.
O Surf Inn não é clube de gringo. Metade da mesa fala português, os mestres são daqui, e feriado é temporada alta de amizade. Carnaval, Tiradentes, réveillon, férias de julho. Escapada de fim de semana ou temporada inteira: chega mais.

## About us

URL: https://surfinn-beta.vercel.app/about-us/

ABOUT US
We are beyond the surf camp business.
We're here to make memories. Surf is the best way we know to start one.
MEET LUCAS
Why Surf Inn exists
Lucas started Surf Inn so that a week in Brazil would feel like living here, not visiting. We're Brazilian, and we host the Brazilian way: you don't check in, you're welcomed in.
OUR PILLARS
What our hearts beat for
Surf
Three students max per coach, surf guiding, video analysis, and a rack of boards for every level.
Music
Samba reggae on Tuesdays, capoeira on Wednesdays, and live music whenever it starts, which is often.
Community
Travel is mostly about the people you meet. Here, everyone makes friends quickly and easily: guests, coaches and neighbors.
Wellbeing

### Questions and answers

Q: Do I need a visa?
A: Most European and UK passports enter Brazil visa-free for up to 90 days. Since 10 April 2025, US, Canadian and Australian passports need an e-visa. Check your country's current agreement before booking flights.

Q: What should I pack?
A: Boardshorts or bikini, a lycra, reef-safe sunscreen, something for warm evenings. Boards and wetsuits live at the camp.

Q: Is Brazil safe?
A: Our neighborhoods are calm, residential and well known to us. We brief you on arrival with the same advice we'd give a friend, where to go, what to skip.

Q: Rio or Itacaré: which camp should I choose?
A: Rio if you want the city: Recreio's waves, samba, forró and nights out, with Rio's landmarks close by. Itacaré if you want nature: a small town between the jungle and wild beaches, warmer water and a slower pace. Many guests do both.

Q: How do I get to the camp from the airport?
A: For Rio, fly into GIG or SDU: the camp is about 50 minutes from GIG. For Itacaré, fly into Ilhéus (IOS), then about 1h15 by road. We arrange door-to-door transfers, and someone waits with your name when you land.

Q: Can I stay without taking any lessons?
A: Absolutely. A bed and the big table make a full stay, add activities whenever you like, including once you're here.

Q: What are meals like?
A: Breakfast is available at the camp (included in Itacaré, optional in Rio); for other meals we point you to our favorite local spots, or, in Rio, the kitchen is yours.

Q: Is there wifi?
A: Yes, good enough that guests work remotely for weeks. See the "Who it's for" page for the honest details.

Q: What if the ocean is flat?
A: Surfskate, SUP, hikes, fishing, capoeira, percussion classes. Flat days are a feature, not a bug.

Q: Can I bring my own board?
A: Of course, and airlines to Brazil are generally board-friendly. Or travel light and use our quiver.

Q: When is the best time to surf in Rio and Itacaré?
A: Both camps have waves all year. In Rio, April to June is the sweet spot, July to September brings the biggest swell, and December to March is small and sunny, perfect for learning. In Itacaré, July to September has the most consistent swell and summer is beginner heaven.

Q: How many days does it take to learn to surf?
A: Most guests ride their first wave on day one. To really progress, plan a week: our Surf Intensive package has 8 lessons over 7 nights, three students max per coach.

Q: How warm is the water? Do I need a wetsuit?
A: In Itacaré the water is 25°C or more all year: boardshorts or bikini, twelve months a year. In Rio it reaches 26°C in summer; on winter mornings a thin top or a shorty helps, and the camp has them.

Q: How much does a stay cost?
A: Packages start from €185 for 3 nights in Rio and from €170 in Itacaré, in a shared room in low season. Prices move with season and availability: our local team sends the exact price with your quote, and no payment happens online.

Q: Is my request a commitment?
A: No. The funnel sends your wishes to a human who gets back to you as soon as possible. You decide after the quote.

Q: Can we book as a group?
A: Yes, friend trips, couples, retreats. Tell us the headcount and we'll take it from there.
